name: Archaeological Site of Delphi
description: Perched on the steep southwestern slope of Mount Parnassus in central Greece, Delphi was where ancient Greeks came to consult the Pythia, the priestess who spoke for Apollo. They believed the world's centre lay here, marked by a carved stone called the omphalos, or "navel." Today you can wander the ruined sanctuary's monuments, built by rival city-states, amid dramatic mountain scenery.
